La demanda dice cuánto se quiere comprar: Demand says how much people want to buy at each price and falls as the price rises; supply says how much they want to sell, and rises with the price. The equilibrium is the price $P^*$ at which the two quantities coincide: there is neither surplus nor shortage.
$Q_d = a − b P$ &emsp; $Q_s = c + d P$ &: $Q_d = a − b P$   $Q_s = c + d P$   $P^* = {a − c}/{b + d}$
Un precio máximo por debajo del de equil: A price ceiling below the equilibrium price causes a shortage: people want to buy more than is offered (queues, black market). A price floor above it causes a surplus: more is offered than is bought (the government buys the excess, or there is unemployment if it is the minimum wage). In both cases the smaller of the two quantities is traded.
Si cambia algo que no es el precio, la c: If something other than the price changes, the whole curve moves. Demand increases with income (normal goods), tastes, population or when a substitute gets more expensive; supply increases if costs fall or technology improves, and decreases with a bad harvest or when raw materials get more expensive. More demand raises the price and the quantity; more supply lowers the price and raises the quantity.
